title: 88-level condition name — a named constant that tests its parent field for one or more values
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. STATUS-FLAGS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-STATE   PIC X.
           88  IS-OPEN    VALUE "O".
           88  IS-CLOSED  VALUE "C".
           88  IS-PENDING VALUE "P" "W".
      *> 88-level names are CONDITIONS, not fields. IF IS-OPEN is a
      *> readable shorthand for IF WS-STATE = "O". SET IS-OPEN TO
      *> TRUE writes "O" to WS-STATE. Naive Java port that defines
      *> isOpen as a boolean misses the round-trip: the 88-level
      *> sets back to the parent field.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           SET IS-OPEN TO TRUE.
           IF IS-PENDING DISPLAY "pending".
           STOP RUN.
notes: 88-level conditions are everywhere in COBOL business logic. They look like booleans but they're actually a syntactic shorthand for value comparison on the parent field. A Java rewrite to an enum is the natural target; the spec must capture the value mappings.
